source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED conflates Set User Access with username, password, credential rotation and account enablement while correctly requiring a dedicated identity, readback, least privilege and rollback.

old_problem: The historical review correctly protected production accounts but treated standard request fields and credential lifecycle as unknown vendor semantics. IPMI Set User Access contains no username or password and, under current errata semantics, user enable/disable is handled by Set User Password. App 43h can change only the selected user's per-channel privilege while preserving callback/link/IPMI access bits and omitting the optional unreadable session-limit field. Requiring credential mutation therefore falsely blocked a bounded standard test and risked merging three separate source identities.
disposition_reason: Use one pre-provisioned disposable non-null, non-production test User ID on one exact channel. Capture App 44h access state, channel privilege ceiling, username/enable status and all-user digest; ensure no active session uses the test identity. Send App 43h with byte-1 bit 7 clear so callback/link/IPMI access flags do not change, omit optional byte 4 so simultaneous-session policy does not change, and lower only byte 3 privilege from an approved Operator/Administrator baseline to User 02h. Read back, establish a fresh User-level session and perform one harmless read, close it, restore the original privilege through the independent control identity, and prove all other account/channel/credential state unchanged. No name, password, enable, access-bit, session-limit, Administrator grant, bulk-user or log operation is part of this row.
decision_basis: Master XLSX rows 1023-1026, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT second review, tests_gpt_merged, selection manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. The exact code is unique. Formal queue sequence 62 was independently verified as row 1026 / variant 8d97ab9624f04d47.

IPMI v2.0 section 22.26 defines App NetFn 06h command 43h for the privilege level and channel accessibility of one User ID. Byte 1 selects the channel and its bit 7 controls whether callback/link/IPMI access bits are changed; byte 2 is a six-bit nonzero User ID; byte 3 is the per-channel User Privilege Limit.

With byte-1 bit 7 equal to zero, callback restriction, link authentication and IPMI Messaging flags are explicitly not changed. This permits a privilege-only conformance test without toggling account reachability.

Optional byte 4 sets a simultaneous-session limit but Get User Access does not return that value, and unsupported nonzero input returns CCh. Omitting byte 4 is therefore required to avoid an unobservable policy mutation and preserve Coverage boundaries.

Privilege values are Callback 1h, User 2h, Operator 3h, Administrator 4h, OEM 5h and No Access Fh. The test only lowers an existing dedicated test-account limit to User 02h and later restores the exact captured value; it never grants a higher privilege.

Section 22.27 App 44h returns user-slot counts, enable status, fixed-name count, callback/link/IPMI flags and the selected user's privilege. Set User Access success alone is insufficient, and the implementation may not report that the user privilege exceeds the channel ceiling, so Get Channel Access must independently prove the effective ceiling.

Changed access/privilege may take effect only on the user's next session. The test requires no existing session for the dedicated identity and uses a newly established session after the write; it does not terminate or reinterpret unrelated sessions.

Set User Name 45h, Get User Name 46h and Set User Password 47h are distinct adjacent source identities. This case must not change or claim their username/password/enable coverage, and no credential rotation is needed unless evidence exposure occurs.

ED-02/ED-03/ED-13 allow exact standard BMC behavior without OEM guesses; ED-15 governs authoritative unsupported N/A; ED-18/ED-30 require authorization and least privilege; ED-19 preserves security evidence; ED-28 requires isolation/recovery; ED-33 through ED-38 govern package readiness, confirmation, cleanup, non-retry and engineer verdict separation.

test_case.test_name: IPMI Set User Access (App 06h/43h) dedicated-user privilege-only downgrade and exact restore
test_case.purpose: Validate the standard per-user, per-channel privilege write by temporarily lowering only one disposable test User ID to User level, proving exact readback and fresh-session behavior, then restoring its original privilege without changing access flags, session limits, name, password, enable status or any other account.
required_package: Approved BMC/firmware and exact numeric session-based channel with App 43h/44h support, plus Get Channel Access evidence for the channel privilege ceiling
Pre-provisioned dedicated nonzero User ID that is not User 1/null, production, root, shared or the independent control/recovery administrator; immutable mapping to its redacted username and owner

Baseline App 44h response, Get User Name hash, enable status, callback/link/IPMI flags, privilege and all-user/channel digest; original privilege must be Operator 03h or Administrator 04h and no active session may use the test identity
Protected existing credential for the dedicated identity solely to establish the post-change User session; no Set User Name/Password, enable/disable or secret logging

Validated secret-safe App 43h/44h runner or upstream-equivalent `user priv` implementation with explicit channel/User ID, omitted session-limit byte, completion/readback parser, exact restore and zero automatic retries
Independent approved Administrator control identity/path, immediate security point confirmation and exact original-privilege recovery payload
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED SECURITY-CONFIGURATION PROCEDURE; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Preserve audit/SEL and do not clear logs. Through the independent control identity, verify BMC/channel, Get Channel Access ceiling and the dedicated TEST_USER_ID; require TEST_USER_ID in 02h..3Fh, no active session for it, original App 44h access byte/privilege BASE_PRIV in {03h,04h}, and immutable username/enable/all-user baselines. Display exact target and obtain immediate approval. Send exactly once App 06h/43h with three request bytes [TARGET_CHANNEL with bit7=0 and bits6:4=0, TEST_USER_ID with bits7:6=0, 02h]. Do not send optional byte 4. Require completion 00h. Read App 44h and require identical counts/enable/callback/link/IPMI fields with privilege 02h; independently verify Get User Name hash and channel ceiling unchanged. Establish a fresh session using the protected dedicated credential at User level, issue only Get Device ID, verify no privilege above User is claimed, then close that session. In a finally path, send exactly once the same three-byte 43h request with BASE_PRIV, require 00h, read App 44h/Get User Name/channel state and require exact baseline, and verify no unrelated user/session/audit change. Never target User 1, a production/recovery account, set access bits, include session limit, write name/password/enable state, grant privilege, enumerate-write multiple users, expose a secret, clear logs or automatically retry.
test_case.expected_result: The single privilege-only 43h request returns 00h. App 44h shows only the dedicated user's per-channel privilege changed to User 02h; maximum/enabled/fixed user counts, enable status, callback/link/IPMI flags, username hash, password/credential, session-limit policy, channel ceiling and all unrelated users remain unchanged. A fresh User session performs Get Device ID and closes. The single restore returns 00h and all observed fields match the original baseline exactly. Any generic/CCh failure, wrong User ID/channel, changed access/count/name/enable/credential state, ineffective fresh-session behavior, unexpected privilege, timeout, secret exposure or failed restore is FAIL/NOT READY without retry; authoritative support for only the null user or no disposable configurable User ID permits N/A.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact Source Key/variant, approved dedicated User ID/channel, no preexisting test-user session, complete baseline, one three-byte bit7=0 privilege-only 43h write to 02h, 00h completion, field-exact 44h readback, fresh User-level harmless read, exact original privilege restore and proof that name/password/enable/access/session-limit/channel/other-user/audit state never changed. A `channel setaccess` operation that changes callback/link/IPMI flags, any Set User Name/Password call, User 1 or production/admin/recovery target, optional byte 4, privilege increase, only a success code without readback, current-session-only test, CCh, hidden retry, secret logging, unrelated session closure, log clearing or incomplete restoration cannot pass. Missing account/baseline/credential/control path is NOT READY rather than Pending review.
safety_gate: Target one pre-provisioned disposable User ID only. Exclude User 1/null, built-in/fixed production identities, shared/root/admin recovery accounts and any identity with active sessions.
Use byte-1 bit 7 = 0 so callback/link/IPMI access flags remain unchanged, and omit optional byte 4. Only byte 3 privilege may change, first downward to User and then back to the captured baseline.
Use an independent Administrator control identity/path for write, readback and recovery. The dedicated test identity is used only for one post-change User session and a harmless read.
Do not touch username, password, enabled status or credentials in this row. Protect the existing credential via secret input, never command-line/log it, and revoke only if exposure is detected.
Preserve audit/security logs and hash the all-user/channel baseline without disclosing usernames or secrets. Do not clear logs or close unrelated sessions.

No automatic retry. On timeout, reconcile with App 44h using the independent control path and perform only the exact restore once if needed; stop on wrong-user, privilege, access, enable, login or audit behavior.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant, BMC/firmware/channel, App 43h/44h capability and channel privilege ceiling
Security approval; redacted dedicated User ID ownership/non-production proof; independent control/recovery identity and no-active-test-session evidence
Immutable App 44h/Get User Name/all-user baseline with counts, enable, callback/link/IPMI flags, BASE_PRIV and hashes but no credentials
Redacted exact three-byte privilege-only 43h request, 00h response and 44h comparison proving only privilege 02h changed
Fresh User session Get Device ID and exact close, with protected secret handling and no higher-privilege action
Single restore request/response, exact baseline equality for user/channel/other identities/sessions/audit, cleanup and engineer PASS/FAIL/NOT READY/N/A authority
test_case.recovery: The normal rollback is one precomputed three-byte App 43h request for the same exact channel/User ID with byte-1 bit7=0 and byte3 BASE_PRIV, followed by App 44h, Get User Name and all-user/channel comparisons. On an ambiguous response, do not resend the change; query through the independent Administrator path, then restore only if the observed privilege differs. If the wrong user or any access/name/enable/credential field changes, stop, preserve audit evidence and have the security owner restore that exact identity from the immutable baseline using the correct separate command. Revoke/rotate the dedicated credential only on exposure. Confirm no active test session and no unrelated-user drift before closure.

source_conflict.reason: Official sections 22.26-22.27 define the exact user/channel/access/privilege schema and show that username, password and enable state are separate commands. The review-layer procedure replaces TBD without merging adjacent coverage and excludes unsafe generic log clearing.

blocked.reason: Core Set/Get User Access semantics, a privilege-only payload and a verifiable restore are standardized. Dedicated User ID, channel, baseline, credential and recovery identity are finite Project prerequisites rather than unresolved engineering decisions.

project_authority: The Project security/BMC owners designate the disposable User ID/channel, approve the downward User transition and baseline restore, protect the existing credential, validate the runner and issue the verdict. They may approve N/A only with authoritative evidence that the platform exposes no configurable non-null test User ID. Approval cannot target production/recovery identities, mutate access/name/password/enable/session-limit fields, grant higher privilege, merge adjacent command coverage, retry automatically, clear logs or accept incomplete restoration.
